chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from someone else, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Yaqub ibn Shu'ayb and Ubayd ibn Zurara, who said:

We asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who sold foodstuff for dirhams for a specified term. When that term arrived, he (the buyer) demanded payment, so he (the seller) said, 'I do not have dirhams with me; take foodstuff from me.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'There is no problem with it. Rather, he has dirhams; he may take whatever he wishes with them.'

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: There is no problem with it / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to pay a cash debt with goods instead of money in Islam?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the permissibility of settling a monetary debt with goods (in-kind payment) when the debtor lacks cash, a practice known as 'sarf' or debt settlement. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) emphasizes the creditor's autonomy, confirming that since the debt is denominated in dirhams, the buyer retains the right to choose between accepting the goods or demanding cash to purchase whatever he desires. This ruling underscores the flexibility in commercial transactions within Shia jurisprudence, prioritizing the creditor's preference to avoid hardship.
